I will keep to the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation on most of my land, because in Quzhou County that is the safest way for me to keep stable yield and income. I know this system, the local weather fits it, and the irrigation and machinery are familiar to me. At the start of the growing season, the winter wheat is already in the field, so my first job is to push wheat management well: one strong topdressing at jointing, careful watering depending on soil moisture, and disease and insect control only when pressure shows up. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize with improved or hybrid seed, because the stubble timing is tight and I need a crop that emerges fast, stands well, and can handle heat. On a smaller piece, I will plant peanuts in spring to spread risk and keep some cash income outside the grain rotation. I will not make the farm too complicated, because I rely on practical routines and I want work that I can manage steadily through the whole year.

For management, I will keep fertilizer moderate and targeted rather than excessive. On wheat, I will use more nitrogen because that crop responds well here, with phosphorus and potassium as base fertilizer, rotary tillage already done before sowing and field leveling kept good for irrigation. I will water wheat about three times in a normal year: around jointing, booting or heading, and grain filling if moisture is short. I will spray two to three times depending on weeds, rust, aphids, and scab risk. For summer maize, I will use one-pass seeding after wheat harvest, mostly no-tillage into wheat stubble to save time and protect moisture, with enough nitrogen for strong growth and fewer irrigations unless the summer rains fail. I will spray for weeds early and then control armyworm, corn borer, or disease if needed. For peanuts, I will plough the small plot, use less nitrogen and more balanced phosphorus and potassium, and keep irrigation lighter. This is the plan I would actually follow because it matches my land, labor, and the way I farm for dependable output.
